questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The inverse of the statement $(\mathrm{p} \wedge \sim \mathrm{q}) \rightarrow \mathrm{r}$ is
questions.solution: The inverse of the proposition $(\mathrm{p} \wedge \sim \mathrm{q})\rightarrow \mathrm{r}$ is $\begin{aligned} \sim( \mathrm{p} \wedge \sim \mathrm{q}) \rightarrow \sim \mathrm{r} \equiv \sim \mathrm{p} \vee \sim(\sim \mathrm{q}) \rightarrow \sim \mathrm{r}\\ \equiv \sim \mathrm{p} \vee \mathrm{q} \rightarrow \sim \mathrm{r} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Negation of the proposition : If we control population growth, we prosper
options: If we do not control population growth, we prosper
If we control population growth, we do not prosper
We control population but we do not prosper
We do not control population, but we prosper
questions.solution: $\mathrm{p}$ : we control population, $\mathrm{q}$ : we prosper $\therefore$ we have $\mathrm{p} \Rightarrow \mathrm{q}$ Its negation is $\sim(\mathrm{p} \Rightarrow \mathrm{q})$ i.e. $\mathrm{p} \wedge \sim \mathrm{q}$ i.e., we control population but we do not prosper.
